profiles.meeting_scenario: JetBrains is preparing an internal dogfood rollout of an updated context-composing pipeline for Full Line Code Completion in PyCharm. The update adds richer prompt context signals for Python files, including sibling-file snippets, import graph summaries, and notebook-cell boundaries, and it requires coordination between the IDE-side integration and the model-serving stack. The meeting agenda is to align on the request interface, confirm which model endpoint will receive the new payload, verify what 'backward compatible' means for older IDE builds still used internally, and agree on what must be finished before enabling the feature flag for Friday's dogfood cohort. The expected outcome is a shared understanding of the handoff: what the IDE team will emit, what the ML service will accept, which environment will be used, and what counts as being ready to turn the feature on.

members.name: Elena Petrova
members.expertise: IDE completion pipeline integration, IntelliJ Platform request serialization, feature-flagged rollout coordination
members.background: Elena has spent four years on JetBrains editor infrastructure and recently took ownership of wiring Full Line Code Completion requests from the IDE client into the shared inference gateway for Python.
members.private_state: She wants to keep the client-side change minimal so it can safely land in the 2025.1 branch without destabilizing editor latency or forcing support work for older internal builds.
hidden_assumptions: The 'context bundle' is the final client payload after IDE-side relevance filtering and token-budget truncation, because that is the artifact her code actually constructs.
When people say the 'current model' in rollout conversations, they mean the production-backed Python endpoint already wired behind the existing internal feature flag.
A schema is 'backward compatible' if older IDE builds can keep sending their old request shape and the server simply tolerates missing newer fields.
'Dogfood-ready by Friday' means the IDE integration is merged, the feature flag can be enabled for employees, and no blocking client exceptions remain.

members.name: Marcus Lin
members.expertise: Transformer prompting, context composition, inference services, offline replay evaluation
members.background: Marcus works on the server-side context composer and model-serving stack for Full Line Code Completion, and he recently finished experiments showing gains from richer structural context in Python files.
members.private_state: He wants the new context fields adopted broadly enough to validate his latest composer changes in realistic traffic, but he is worried that silently missing fields will make the rollout data hard to interpret.
hidden_assumptions: The 'context bundle' is the raw set of retrieved context pieces before final packing into the model token window, because server-side composition now decides what survives truncation.
The 'current model' refers to the latest canary checkpoint used in the team's evaluation deck, since that is the model he is actively tuning and discussing daily.
A schema is only meaningfully 'backward compatible' if requests missing the new fields still lead to essentially equivalent behavior because the server can reconstruct sensible defaults.
'Dogfood-ready by Friday' includes enough replay and dashboard instrumentation to tell whether the new context signals are actually being delivered and helping.
When the IDE sends additional context, it should preserve as much raw material as possible, because the server-side composer is now the authoritative place for token-budget decisions.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss sending the 'context bundle' to the model service.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the final serialized request payload after the IDE has already ranked, deduplicated, and truncated snippets to fit the token budget.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the larger raw package of candidate context items that the server-side composer will later rank and trim before prompt construction.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are used to collapsing several pipeline stages into one shorthand term, and the meeting is about coordination rather than architecture, so 'bundle' sounds precise enough to neither side.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the new payload should work with the 'current model'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the production-like endpoint `py-fllm-4.2` already used in the existing internal rollout path.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the canary model `ctxcomp-v5-canary` discussed in the latest offline evaluation results and available in staging.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Each person's day-to-day work has a different default reference for 'current', and because both endpoints are live somewhere in the system, the phrase feels naturally unambiguous in context.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the request schema should stay 'backward compatible'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means older IDE builds can still send requests without the new fields and the server will accept them without errors or client changes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means older requests should still yield roughly comparable suggestions because the server can infer or default the missing signals well enough for evaluation continuity.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Backward compatibility is treated as routine engineering hygiene, so neither person expects it to conceal different success thresholds: one is focused on protocol acceptance, the other on behavioral equivalence.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on being 'dogfood-ready by Friday'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes client integration merged, the flag enabled for internal users, and no blocking IDE-side regressions.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 includes those items plus replay validation and an acceptance dashboard showing the new context fields are arriving and affecting suggestions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Readiness language in coordination meetings often compresses technical and operational work into one phrase, and each side assumes the omitted pieces are obviously inside or outside the boundary based on role.
